title: Nuclear radiation and conservation in decay practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: Original radiation, field and decay contexts test the mapped demands without copying official wording, values or diagrams. P1 remains deferred and unassigned.

questions.prompt: In the nuclide notation ^{41}_{19}K, state the proton number and the number of neutrons.
Which row describes an alpha particle?

options.A: two protons and two neutrons, charge +2e

questions.prompt: A beta-minus particle and a beta-plus particle are compared. Which statement is correct?

options.A: They have equal charge and different masses.
options.B: They have opposite charges and approximately equal masses.
options.D: They are both uncharged electromagnetic radiation.

questions.prompt: A nucleus emits a beta-minus particle. What happens to the daughter's nucleon number A and proton number Z?

options.A: A decreases by 4 and Z decreases by 2
options.B: A is unchanged and Z decreases by 1
options.C: A is unchanged and Z increases by 1
options.D: A and Z are both unchanged

questions.prompt: A narrow beam contains alpha radiation and gamma radiation. It passes between two oppositely charged parallel plates.

figure.purpose: Assess use of charge to distinguish alpha from gamma radiation.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white Cambridge-inspired diagram with a mixed beam entering between parallel plates. Mark the upper plate positive and lower plate negative. Show a straight outgoing path labelled P and a gently downward-curved path labelled Q. Do not identify the radiations or annotate forces.
figure.alt_text: A mixed radiation beam separates into a straight path and a path curved toward a negative plate.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Identify which path is followed by alpha radiation and which is followed by gamma radiation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain the difference between the two paths using the charge of each radiation.

questions.prompt: Complete and check two nuclear decay equations.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Polonium-210 undergoes alpha decay. Complete ^{210}_{84}Po -> ^A_ZPb + ^4_2He by determining A and Z, then show both conservation checks.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Carbon-14 undergoes beta-minus decay. Complete ^{14}_{6}C -> ^A_ZN + ^0_{-1}e by determining A and Z, then show both conservation checks.

questions.prompt: An unknown nuclide X contains 88 protons and 138 neutrons. It emits an alpha particle to form Y. Nuclide Y then emits a beta-minus particle to form Z.

figure.purpose: Assess a mixed chain from prior nuclide bookkeeping into current decay conservation.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white Cambridge-inspired two-stage chain X to Y to Z. Label the first arrow alpha and the second beta-minus. Under X show only 88 protons and 138 neutrons. Leave upper and lower nuclide-number boxes for X, Y and Z blank. Do not provide answers.
figure.alt_text: An unknown nucleus emits alpha radiation and its daughter then emits beta-minus radiation.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Determine the nucleon number of X and write X as ^A_ZX.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Determine the nucleon number and proton number of Y.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Determine the nucleon number and proton number of Z.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Use your values to check that charge is conserved across both stages together.
